lines.text: One treaty has phased out nearly 99 percent of the ozone-destroying chemicals it banned.
And not a single country stayed out.
The Montreal Protocol was signed on September 16th, 1987.
Its main target: CFCs, from fridges and spray cans.
In the stratosphere, sunlight splits them, and their chlorine destroys ozone, again and again.
In 2009 it became the first UN treaty ratified by every country.
Ozone is on track to recover to 1980 levels around 2040 for most of the world, 2045 over the Arctic, and 2066 over Antarctica.
Their substitutes, HFCs, spare the ozone but heat the planet.
So in 2016 the Kigali Amendment set out to phase them down.
But the Antarctic hole still opens every spring.
So, was the ozone layer a one-off?
Or proof the world can act, again?
